_comment: An EXAMPLE of routes, not loaded by the daemon (engine_seam.ACTIONS_PATHS
does not list it). It shows the shape a flow takes when the driver points
a task page somewhere instead of only approving or continuing it.
A route is an ordinary action. Its trigger is the `task:route` command the
surface bridge writes when the driver picks `route:<name>` on a page; its
body is whatever that route activates. The node that built the page is
told which routes listen for it (runnerlib/tasks.routes_for) and offers
the ones that fit as extra choices on its verdict form.
The flow here: the `task` node's page can be routed to `review`, which
spawns a `review` node on the same task key. The review node's page gets
its own feedback action, so `continue` on it goes back through review —
not through task. To use it for real: register a `review` node and add
The route the daemon DOES load is config/actions-routes.json: approve a
page and hand it to the `implement` node, which carries it out.

actions.name: task-routed-to-review
actions._why: a fresh reviewer reads the page this task produced and judges it

actions.name: review-feedback-resumes-review
actions._why: continue on a review page goes back through the review node

payload.note: driver feedback is the next review turn
